title: Armistice 2022
subtitle: WOD for Warriors Tribute by Team RWB
workout:
For Time
6 Rounds of:
11 Mountain Climbers
11 Power Cleans (95/65 lb)

Rest 2 minutes

Then, 6 Rounds of:
19 Hand Release Push-Ups
18 Box Jump Burpees
100 meter Run
description:
Background: Veterans Day has been observed since 1954 by the U.S., and its origins date back to Armistice Day 1918, which marked the cessation of hostilities on the Western Front in WWI. Veterans Day preserves the historical significance of the 11/11/1918, but also focuses attention on the important purpose of Veterans Day: A celebration to honor America’s veterans for their patriotism, love of country, and willingness to serve and sacrifice for the common good. WOD for Warriors is held yearly on the 11th month, 11th day and 11th hour to celebrate the service of all U.S. military Veterans in a meaningful way within their own communities.

WOD for Warriors is a functional fitness tribute workout held once a year on Veterans Day at gyms all throughout the country. WOD for Warriors supports Team Red, White and Blue @teamrwb, whose mission is to enrich the lives of America’s veterans by connecting them to their communities through physical and social activity.

This WOD is designed to celebrate the service of all U.S. military veterans in a meaningful way by providing an opportunity for veterans and non-veterans to meet and sweat with members of their community through functional fitness on a national level with the goal of fundraising for Team RWB’s Veteran enriching programs.

The 6 rounds represent each branch of the military: Army, Navy, Marines, Air Force, Coast Guard, and Space Force. Each exercise's count represents the 11th day of the 11th month of 1918, Armistice Day, which is now known as Veterans Day.

At the 11th hour on the 11th day of the 11th month, color guards representing each branch of the military render honors during a ceremony at the tomb of the unknown soldiers at Arlington National Cemetery. The 2 minutes between each set of workouts represents a time of rest/reflection honoring the unknown soldiers during this WOD.

See also: All Team RWB "Armistice" WODs
notes:
With a running clock, completed the prescribed work as fast as possible ("For Time"). Start with 6 rounds of 11 Mountain Climbers and 11 Power Cleans. Rest for 2 minutes to reflect. Then proceed to the next 6 rounds of 19 Hand Release Push-Ups, 18 Box Jump Burpees, and 100 meter Run.

Score is the time on the clock when the last round of the Run is completed.

title: BCS Classic 22.1
subtitle: 2022 BCS Classic WOD #1
workout:
AMRAP in 15 minutes (with a Partner)
36 Squat Cleans (135/95 lb)
16 Synchro Burpee Box Jump Overs (24/20 in)
30 Squat Cleans (185/125 lb)
16 Synchro Burpee Box Jump Overs (24/20 in)
24 Squat Cleans (225/155 lb)
16 Synchro Burpee Box Jump Overs (24/20 in)

In the remaining time, AMRAP of:
Squat Cleans (245/165 lb)
description: Background: “BCS Classic 22.1” was the 2nd of 4 total WODs for the 2022 BCS Classic competition held on August 27-28, 2022 at the Brazos County Expo Center.
notes:
Both Athletes will start behind their designated Barbell.  At the call of 3-2-1 GO, athletes will begin their first round of Squat Cleans.  Athletes may alternate the Squat Clean reps however they like, as long as the complete the required amount total reps.  Athletes will then move to the Synchro Burpee Box Jump Overs.  Athletes will required to complete this movement synchronized.

Both athletes chest and thighs must be touching the ground at the bottom of the Burpee and they must be perpendicular to the Plyo Box.  Both athletes  must have all their feet on top of the Plyo Boxes together before jumping/ stepping off the opposite side.  If one athlete jumps/ steps off the Box before their partner does, the team will be given a no rep and be required to return to the top of the Box.

Athletes will continue this pattern of movements until they reach the final Squat Clean weight for max reps or they hit the time cap. 

Score is the total number of repetitions completed before the 15-minute clock stops.

Movement Standards

Squat Clean: The Barbell begins on the ground. Touch and go is permitted. No bouncing or dropping and catching the Barbell on the rebound. Once dropped, the Barbell must settle on the ground before the athlete begins the next repetition. The athlete must pass through a full squat with hips below the knees. Receiving the Barbell in the bottom of the squat is not required; a Power Clean or Split Clean followed by a front squat will be permitted, but a deadlift followed by a Hang Clean is not allowed. 

The rep is credited when the athlete’s hips and knees are fully extended, and the bar is resting on the shoulders with the elbows in front of the Bar.

Synchro Burpee Box Jump Over: The Burpee Box Jump Over starts with the athlete facing the Box while touching the chest and thighs to the ground and finishes with the athlete jumping over the Box. In the bottom position, to ensure the athlete remains perpendicular to the Box on each rep, the athlete’s shoulders must remain perpendicular to the Box, while on the ground. For the synchronized burpee to count, both athletes’ chests must be on the ground at the same time.

There is no requirement to stand tall while on top of the Box. A two-foot takeoff is always required, and only the athlete’s feet may touch the Box. The athlete may jump on top of the Box using a two-foot landing and then jump or step off to the other side, or the athlete may jump completely over the Box. If jumping over the Box, the feet must go over the Box, not around it, and the athlete must use a two-foot landing. Each rep is counted when both athletes have landed on the ground on the opposite side, where they may begin their next rep. 

Scaling Options

Intermediate
AMRAP in 15 minutes (with a Partner)
36 Squat Cleans (115/75 lb)
16 Synchro Burpee Box Jump Overs (24/20 in)
30 Squat Cleans (135/105 lb)
16 Synchro Burpee Box Jump Overs (24/20 in)
24 Squat Cleans (155/125 lb)
16 Synchro Burpee Box Jump Overs (24/20 in)

In the remaining time, AMRAP of:
Squat Cleans (185/145 lb)

Scaled

title: DOUBLE DOWN
subtitle: ATHENA Daily WOD
workout:
AMRAP in 13 minutes
45 Double-Unders
13 Hang Power Snatches (75/55 lb)
3 Wall Walks
notes:
Today we have a combination of skill movements, plus a technical barbell movement, santch.

Double-Unders: Love or hate them, they are here to stay. These 45 reps should take no longer than 60 seconds. If you are working on proficiency, complete as many Double-Under as you can in 60 seconds each round. If you are new or still working on mastering your Double-Unders. Pick the hardest scaling option from below that will take you 60 seconds or less.

Snatches: These should feel relatively light. If you can do 13 Power Snatches unbroken at the workout weight when fresh, then complete this version as written (Rx). Otherwise, pick a load you can complete 13 Power Snatches unbroken when fresh. Target hitting “triple extension” (ankles, knees and hips all extended and locking out at the same time) before starting the pull with your arms.

Wall Walks: Developing this skill is a mix of overhead pressing, core stability and balance. If you can complete 3 wall walks in under 3 minutes, complete this movement as written. If not, pick the most challenging scaling option from below.

INSTRUCTIONS

On a 13-minute clock, perform as many rounds and repetitions as possible (“AMRAP”) of the Double-Unders, Hang Power Santches, and Wall Walks.

Record your score as the total number of Rounds + Repetitions completed before the 13-minute clock stops.

SCALING OPTIONS

DOUBLE-UNDERS
- If you have 10-15 Double Unders but they are not consistent, perform 1 minute of Double-Under attempts per round.
- If your Double Unders are hit or miss, complete double the reps of Single-Unders AND 5 Double-Under attempts each round.
- If your Double Unders are not yet developed, complete double the reps of Single-Unders.

workout:

description: Background: “RI Online Qualifier 22.2” was the 2nd of 4 total WODs for the 2022 Rogue Invitational Online Qualifiers competition. Minimum of 5 male and 5 female competitions will qualify for the in-person competition taking place in October.
notes:
The athlete will start seated on the rower with their feet in the straps and the handle in the stowed position. At the call of 3-2-1-Go the athlete will begin rowing 30/25 calories. When the screen reads 0 the athlete will move to the Handstand Push-Up position and complete 9 Strict Handstand Push-Ups (SHSPU). Upon completion they will return to the Rower and complete 30/25 cal then return and complete 12 SHSPU.

The athlete will then complete 30/25 cal and 15 SHSPU, 30/25 cal and 18 SHSPU and finish with 30/25 cal and 21 SHSPU. When the athlete completes 21 Strict Handstand Push-Ups, their workout is over.

Score is the time on the clock when the last Strict Handstand Push-Up is completed.

Movement Standards

Row: The monitor on the Concept2 Rower must be set to 30/25 Cals and the athlete must stay seated on the Rower until the required calories have been completed. Judges may reset the Rowers between rounds. If Rowing when time is called, the score will be the number of calories completed at the time of the clock - no run over is allowed. 1 repetition will be awarded for every calorie completed.

Strict Handstand Push-Up: Prior to starting, a Box that is 40 inches wide and 24 inches deep must be marked on the floor. Measurements must be to the INSIDE of the tape lines. If any part of the hand, including the fingers, makes contact with the tape the repetition will not be counted. Every repetition of the HandstandPush-Up begins and ends at the top of a handstand with the arms fully locked out, only the heels in contact with the wall, the hips open and the body in line with the arms.

The feet must remain inside the width of the hands throughout the entire repetition. At the bottom, the athlete’s head makes contact with the ground. If the hands are on plates and there is a pad under the head, the top of the pad must be level with the tops of the plates. The feet do not need to remain in contact with the wall for the entire repetition, but athletes must begin and end each repetition with their heels on the wall.

Kipping is not allowed. Any repetition that is assisted by the hips or legs will not count. Only the heels may touch the wall during the repetition. The complete hand, to include the fingers, must stay within the dimensions of the box marked on the ground.

Scaling Options

For Time
30/25 calorie Row
6 Kipping Handstand Push-Ups

30/25 calorie Row
9 Kipping Handstand Push-Ups

30/25 calorie Row
12 Kipping Handstand Push-Ups

30/25 calorie Row
15 Kipping Handstand Push-Ups

30/25 calorie Row
18 Kipping Strict Handstand Push-Ups

subtitle: ATHENA WOD

notes:
Your starting weight should be the weight you worked up to in the previous Pause Squat piece.

Focus on bracing your core, driving your knees out on the ascent, and chest and elbows high on the drive back up.

The Front Squat will get your heart rate going, especially as time under tension increases with each set.

If you fail a squat, drop the weight to your last completed set and finish the workout at that load to drill your form.

If you fail to complete 2 Front Squats in the minute, skip a round and recover before continuing.

INSTRUCTIONS

Each minute on the minute (“EMOM”) for 10 minutes, complete 2 Front Squats. Increase the weight after every 2 minutes (5 times throughout the entire 10 minute session).

Log your score as the weight (in kilograms or pounds, eg: 100 lb or 45 kg) of the load used for the last set successfully completed.

SCALING OPTIONS

WEIGHT/MOBILITY
- If you struggle to achieve full depth in the Squat (hips below the knees), keep this workout light and complete 5 Front Squats each minute at the same weight. This weight should be something you can complete 5 Reps unbroken each round as you focus on form and depth.

EMOM for 10 minutes
4 Double Dumbbell Front Squats

Increase the weight every 2 minutes (or if you only have one set of Dumbbells, increase the number of repetitions)

NO EQUIPMENT
EMOM for 10 minutes
45 seconds Max Air Squats
15 seconds Rest

Record your score as the total number of air squats completed in 10 minutes.

title: Triple Sec
subtitle: ELEMENT Daily WOD
workout:
5 Rounds for time:
500 meter Row
7 Ring muscle ups
21 Alternating Lunges
notes:
STIMULUS
Duration: Long (17-22 Minutes)
Volume: Moderate (105 reps)
Load: Body weight

Purpose:
We haven't had a pure body weight loading session in a while and we also haven't practiced our ring muscle ups and lunges either. So we'll combine them in a triplet and get our long time domain session in for the week!

White Board Chat:
Maybe not the "Triple Sec" that you were looking for, but an amazing workout nonetheless! Overall, we're looking to complete this one in 17-22 minutes which leaves us with roughly 4-4:30 per round. That being said, we definitely need to keep up the pace and strive for continuous movement throughout! Our row should be consistently under 2:30. If this is going to be a challenge to maintain; especially across 5 rounds, simply dial back the distance to something that we can keep consistent! Moving on to the ring muscle ups, we should be able to complete these in 2-3 quick sets, completing all reps in about 1:00 or less. Athletes working on a more challenging option here can absolutely cut back the reps in order to keep moving and avoid getting totally burned out by round 4. Try to find a challenge here today! Even if ring muscle ups aren't a goal of yours, creating a challenge here will translate to just about every other gymnastics movement we see! Lastly, moving into the alternating lunges, we should be able to complete these pretty smooth and unbroken in about :30. We can absolutely cut the reps here if necessary as well! All in all, a great start to the week!

MODIFICATIONS

VOLUME/LOADING
3 Rounds for time:
500 meter Row
7 Ring muscle up challenging scaling option
21 Alternating Lunges
OR
5 Rounds for time:
250 meter Row
5 Ring muscle up challenging scaling options
14 Alternating Lunges

Or any combination of the above and the written workout depending on what we are working on

LIMITED EQUIPMENT OPTION
5 Rounds for time:
400 meter Run
7 Strict handstand push ups
21 Alternating Lunges

DUMBBELL OPTION
None today!

MOVEMENTS

Row
-If we have an injury or limitation that prevents us from rowing, perform either a 400m run or 30/24 calories on the Assault bike

Ring Muscle up
-If we have an injury or limitation that prevents us from transitioning over the rings, perform false grip ring rows
-If we have an injury or limitation that prevents us from pulling, perform ring dips
-If we have an injury or limitation that prevents us from using one of our arms, perform single dumbbell clean and jerks with the good arm only

Alternating Lunges
-If we have an injury or limitation that prevents us from bending the knee, perform light weighted good mornings
-If we have an injury or limitation that prevents us from full range of motion, perform alternating step ups to a height that is challenging, but offers a pain free range of motion
-If we have an injury or limitation that prevents us from lunging our body weight, perform ring assisted lunges

title: BCS Online Qualifier 22.1
subtitle: 2022 BCS Classic Online Qualifier Event #1
workout:
21-15-9 Reps for Time (with a Partner)
Burpee Box Jump Overs (24/20 in)
Overhead Squats (135/95 lb)
description: Background: This is the 1st of 4 total events for the 2022 BCS Classic Online Qualifiers competition held on June 20-July 1, 2022.
notes:
At the call of 3,2,1 Go the athlete will start at the line of tape marked 3ft from the box. Then the athlete will begin with their 21 Burpee Box Jump Overs (step-up overs are allowed). Upon completion of the Burpee Box Jump Overs, the athlete will complete 21 Overhead Squats. The athlete will complete this sequence of movements for the rounds of 15 reps and 9 reps.  The workout will finish when the athlete finishes the 9th Overhead Squat. 

Score is the time of both athletes on the event.

Movement Standards

Overhead Squat: Barbell must be placed a minimum of 3 ft from the Box. A line of tape must be placed to mark this spot and the Barbell must stay on the opposite side of the tape away from the Box. The hip crease must be below the top of the knee at the bottom. A full Squat Snatch is permitted, but not required, to start the movement if standard depth is achieved. The Barbell must come to full lockout overhead with the hips, knees and arms fully extended, and the Bar directly over the middle of the body. Athletes must show a complete lockout and full extension at the top for the rep to be counted. 

Burpee Box Jump Over: The Burpee Box Jump Over starts with the athlete facing the Box while touching the chest and thighs to the ground and finishes with the athlete jumping over the Box. In the bottom position, to ensure the athlete remains perpendicular to the Box on each rep, the athlete’s shoulders must remain perpendicular to the Box, while on the ground. A line of tape must be placed perpendicular to the box. The line must run the full length of the body with both hands and feet on either side of the line.

There is no requirement to stand tall while on top of the Box. The athlete may jump or step on top of the Box using a two-foot landing and then jump or step off to the other side, or the athlete may jump completely over the Box. If jumping over the Box, the feet must go over the Box, not around it, and the athlete must use a two-foot landing. Each rep is counted when the athlete has landed on the ground on the opposite side, where they may begin their next rep.

title: Turbo Tunnel
subtitle: 2022 Mid-Atlantic CrossFit Challenge Semifinal WOD #6
workout:
For Time
18 Ring Muscle-Ups
15 Front Squats (205/145 lb)
45 foot Front Rack Lunges (205/145 lb)
12 Bar Muscle-Ups
9 Shoulder-to-Overheads (165/115 lb)
45 foot Overhead Lunges (165/115 lb)

Time Cap: 12 minutes
description:
Background: “Turbo Tunnel” is the 6th workout for the 2022 Mid-Atlantic CrossFit Challenge Semifinal competition. 

The Mid-Atlantic CrossFit Challenge is the final qualifying stage for athletes in North America before the 2022 NOBULL CrossFit Games. Top 30 men, top 30 women and top 20 teams in North America who already made it through the Open and Quarterfinals will compete. Only the top 5 of each division will make it to the Games.
notes:
This event begins with the athlete on the start mat. At the sound of the beep, the athlete will move to the Rings and begin accumulating reps of Ring Muscle-Ups. When 18 Ring Muscle-Ups have been completed the athlete will move to the Barbell and begin accumulating reps of Front Squats.  When 15 Front Squats have been completed the athlete will begin lunging towards the center of the floor starting behind the designated line. 

This will be a Front Rack Lunge. When both feet have crossed the designated line the athlete will drop the Bar and move to the rig in the center of the floor to begin accumulating reps of Bar Muscle-Ups. The athlete will use the Pull-Up Bar closest to the start line. When 12 Bar Muscle-Ups have been completed the athlete will move to the Bar in front of the middle rig and begin accumulating reps of shoulder to overhead.

When 9 reps of Shoulder-to-Overhead have been accumulated the athlete will begin lunging towards the finish line. This will be an Overhead Lunge. When both feet have crossed the designated line the athlete will set the Bar down and go over it  to the finish line. When the athlete reaches the finish mat, time stops.

Lunges will be completed in 5 unbroken section. The first section is 5’; section 2, 3, and 4 is 10’; the 5th section is 5’. 

Score is his or her total time for completing the event.

Movement Standards

Ring Muscle-Up: The rep begins with a hang below the rings with arms fully extended (with or without a ‘false grip’) and the feet off the ground. At the top, elbows must be fully locked out while in a support position over the Rings. Control must be shown at the top, pushing away from the Rings before establishing lock out at the top will result in a no-rep. Kipping the Muscle-Up is acceptable, but swings or rolls to support are not permitted.

If consecutive kipping Muscle-Ups are performed, a change of direction below the Rings is required. If the heels rise above the bottom of the Rings during the kip, it is a no rep. Rings will be set at a fixed height, athletes may not adjust the height of the Rings.

Front Squat: The Barbell must be racked on the front of the shoulders. At the top, the hips and knees must be fully extended. Any grip is permitted as long as the Bar is in the front-rack position. At the bottom the hip crease must be below the top of the knee. A full Squat Clean is permitted, but not required, to start the movement if standard depth is achieved.

Front Rack Lunge: Forward motion will only be allowed while the load is being supported in the front rack position. On each Lunge, the trailing knee must make contact with the ground at the bottom. At the top of each step, the athlete must stand with the hips and knees fully extended. If the knee does not touch the ground, or if the next step is initiated (or the weight is dropped) before fully standing up, the athlete will be required to reset to the beginning of the lunge section. Once both feet clearly pass a solid line and the athlete is standing tall, they will receive credit for the Lunge section. A no rep on any portion of the Lunge will result in the athlete moving back to the last completed section.

Bar Muscle-Up: The athlete must begin with or pass through a hang below the Bar, with the arms fully extended and the feet off the ground. Kipping the muscle up is acceptable, but pullovers, rolls to support and glide kips are not permitted. No portion of the foot may rise above the height of the Bar during the kip. The rep is credited when the arms are fully locked out while the athlete is in the support position above the Bar with the shoulders over or in front of the bar.

Athletes must pass through some portion of a dip-to-lockout over the Bar. Only the hands and no other part of the arm may touch the Pull-Up Bar to assist the athlete in completing the rep. Once on top, the hands must stay in contact with the Bar, and athletes must maintain support with their arms. Removing the hands and resting while on top of the Bar is not allowed.

Shoulder-to-Overhead: Each rep begins in the front rack position, with the Barbell on the shoulders. A Shoulder Press, Push Press, Push Jerk or Split Jerk may be used, as long as the elbow, hips and knees are fully extended. The rep is credited once the weight is fully locked out overhead, directly over the middle of the body with the feet in line. If an athlete uses a Split Jerk, their feet must return under the hips and meet the full lockout requirement. Once the movement is completed the athlete must bring the bar down in front of them, failing to do so will make the previous rep a no-rep.

Overhead Lunge: Each Lunge begins with the Barbell overhead, both feet together behind the starting line and the athlete standing tall with hips and knees extended. At the bottom of the Overhead Lunge, the trailing knee must make contact with the ground and the Barbell must be above the height of the athlete’s head. If, during the Lunge, the Barbell comes into contact with or falls below the level of the athlete’s head, the athlete must stop lunging and return to the start of that section.

The rep is credited when the athlete gets both heels across a solid line, with the Barbell in the overhead position and is standing tall with hips and knees fully extended. Stopping with both feet together on the ground is not required, but the knees and hips must reach full extension before initiating the next rep.The athlete must alternate which foot leads for each step. Shuffle steps that progress forward between steps are not allowed. A no rep on any portion of the Lunge will result in the athlete moving back to the last completed section.

title: MACC Mile
subtitle: 2022 Mid-Atlantic CrossFit Challenge Semifinal WOD #4
workout:
4 Rounds for Time
400 meter Trueform
30 Wall Ball Shots (20/14 lb)
20 Chest-to-Bar Pull-Ups
80 foot Tank Push
10 Sandbag to Shoulder (150/100 lb)
80 foot Tank Push

Time Cap: 25 minutes
description:
Background: “MACC Mile” is the 4th workout for the 2022 Mid-Atlantic CrossFit Challenge Semifinal competition. 

The Mid-Atlantic CrossFit Challenge is the final qualifying stage for athletes in North America before the 2022 NOBULL CrossFit Games. Top 30 men, top 30 women and top 20 teams in North America who already made it through the Open and Quarterfinals will compete. Only the top 5 of each division will make it to the Games.
notes:
This event begins with the athlete standing on the TrueForm Runner. At the sound of the beep, the athlete will begin accumulating meters. When 400 meters have been accumulated the athlete will move to the Wall Ball and begin accumulating reps of Wall Ball Shots. When 30 Wall Balls Shots have been completed the athlete will move to the Pull-Up Bar and begin accumulating reps of Chest-to-Bar Pull-Ups.

When 20 Chest-to-Bar Pull-Ups have been completed the athlete will move to the Tank and begin pushing towards the finish line. The athlete will be permitted to use the low bar handles only. When the Tank has completely crossed the designated line the athlete will move to the Sandbag and begin accumulating reps of Sandbag to shoulder. When 10 Sandbag to shoulder have been completed the athlete will move the Sandbag to the next designated section and then return to the Tank.

The athlete will push the Tank back towards the starting mat; again using the low bar handles only. When the Tank has completely crossed the designated line the athlete will move to the TrueForm Runner to start Round 2. The athlete will continue this pattern for 3 more rounds, moving the Sandbag forward after every round. After the Fourth round of Sandbag to shoulder the athlete WILL NOT push the Tank back towards the starting mat; but will instead move to the finish line.  When the athlete reaches the finish mat, time stops.

Score is the time on the clock when the athlete reaches the finish mat.

Movement Standards

TrueForm Runner: The athletes may not touch the monitor. The athlete may push off the front handrails for initial momentum only. Grabbing the handrails during the Run for balance only is allowed. Athletes must remain on the runner until the display reads the work required. The athlete may coast over the required work, but cannot make an attempt to get off the runner until they are past the required work. Athlete must exit the Truform from behind and NOT go under the handrails.

Wall Ball Shot: In the Wall Ball, the Medicine Ball must be taken from the bottom of a squat, hip crease passing clearly below the knee, and thrown to hit the specified target. The center of the Ball must make contact with the target at or above the specified target height. If the Ball hits below or does not hit the target it is a no rep. If the ball hits the ground it must come to a rest before initiating the next rep. Taking the ball from the rebound into the next rep is a no rep.

Chest-to-Bar Pull-Up: This is a standard Chest-to-Bar Pull-Up. Dead hang, kipping or butterfly Pull-Ups are allowed, as long as all the requirements are met. The arms must be fully extended at the bottom. At the top, the chest must clearly come into contact with the Bar, below the collarbone.

Sandbag to Shoulder: The Sandbag will start from the ground where they will move it to their shoulder however they see fit. The athlete must be fully standing with the Sandbag on their shoulder, showing full extension at both the knees and hips before dropping the Sandbag. The athelete must always work within their box and facing the finish line.

description:
Background: This workout is dedicated to the Freedom Riders, civil rights activists who rode interstate buses into the segregated Southern United States in 1961 and subsequent years to challenge the non-enforcement of the United States Supreme Court decisions Morgan v. Virginia (1946) and Boynton v. Virginia (1960), which ruled that segregated public buses were unconstitutional.

The Southern states had ignored the rulings and the federal government did nothing to enforce them. The first Freedom Ride left Washington, D.C. on May 4, 1961, and was scheduled to arrive in New Orleans on May 17. There were 13 original Freedom Riders and, as the movement grew, so did their numbers. By August 1961, there were hundreds of riders.

The workout was designed by Crossfit War Streets @cfwarstreets412 (Pittsburgh, PA, USA) as one of their tribute WODs for the Black History Month celebration.
notes:
From 0:00-1:01, perform the buy-in of 61-second Weighted Wall Sit. Then from 1:01-13:00, complete as many rounds and repetitions as possible ("AMRAP") of 13 calorie Assault Bike, 13 Dumbbell Cleans, 13 Push-Ups, and 13 Dumbbell Shoulder-to-Overheads. Finally from 14:01, complete the cash-out of 61-second Weighted Wall Sit.

Score is the total number of repetitions completed.

workout:

description:
Background: This workout is dedicated to Firefighter Sergeant-Major Jean-François Spelmans, 48 years old, who was killed when an escalator collapsed crushing him while fighting a fire in the Sheraton Hotel on Place Charles Rogier in Brussels on March 16, 2022. Four people were hospitalized as a result of the fire, over 300 customers had to be evacuated overnight.

Sergeant-Major Jean-François Spelmans was born on August 10, 1972, he joined the ranks of the Brussels Fire Brigade in 1999. He served in the 11th company stationed at the Heliport barracks. 

The workout was designed and first performed at CrossFit 1815 Waterloo @crossfit1815 (Waterloo, Belgium) as a tribute to his memory and sacrifice.

The rep signifies:
- 48 reps for his age when he paid the ultimate sacrifice
- 10 rounds for the Group 10 he was part of
- 3-16-22 reps for the date of the incident
- 1 Rope Climb for the son he left behind.
notes:

Then, proceed to complete the 10 rounds of 3 Power Clean-and-Jerks, 16 Box Step-Ups, 22 Sit-Ups, and 1 Rope Climb. Finally, perform the buy-out of 48 Air Squats.

title: Sprint Finish
subtitle: 2021 Battle Cancer Berlin WOD #3
workout:
AMRAP (in a Team of 4) in 9 minutes
10 Wheelbarrow Sprints (in paid)
20 Under Overs
30 Synchro Burpees (all 4 athletes)
40 Synchro Lunges (all 4 athletes)
50 Synchro Sit-Ups (all 4 athletes)

In the remaining time, AMRAP of:
Max Partner Sprints with D-Ball (30/20 kg)
description: Background: “Sprint Finish” was the 3rd of the 4 total WODs for the 2021 Battle Cancer Berlin competition. It was the 5th annual fundraising competition for cancer research and charities.
notes:
Athletes start lying on the ground. On 3, 2, 1 Go, athletes perform 10 Wheelbarrow Sprints in pairs, there and back equals one rep. Once all ten Sprints are completed, in a team of four, 20 Under Overs are completed, with one athlete holding the bridge/tunnel and the others going under and over, athletes can swap around at any point.

All four athletes will then perform 30 Synchro Burpees, 40 Synchro Lunges and 50 Synchro Sit-Ups.

In the remaining time max partner sprints with a D-Ball.

Score is the total number of repetitions completed before the 9-minute clock stops.

Movement Standards

Wheelbarrow Sprint: In pairs, athletes will perform 10 Wheelbarrow Sprints in total. There and back will equal one rep. One athlete will walk on their hands whilst their partner holds their legs, partners can swap before returning back down the lane.

Under Over: One athlete will go on their hands and feet, whilst the other athletes crawl under them and then jump back over. Athletes must crawl under and then jump back over for the rep to count before the next athlete can go. Athletes can swap in and out as they wish.

Synchro Burpee: Standing in one line facing down the lane, all four athletes will perform Synchronised Burpees; athletes will hinge at the hips to perform a Burpee with chest to floor. The synchronisation is at the top of the rep where all four athletes must jump and clap above their head with their hips through and shoulders back.

Synchro Lunge: Standing in pairs facing each other down the lane, all four athletes will perform Synchronised Lunges, stepping forward, bending the front leg to lower the body until the front thigh is parallel to the floor allowing the back knee to tap the floor. The synchronisation is at the top of the rep where athletes are standing tall with hips and knees at full extension.

Synchro Sit-Up: Athletes must sit in pairs facing each other down the lane, and touch the floor behind their heads before sitting up and clapping. The synchronisation is at the top of the rep with athletes clapping. Athletes must stay in sync with each other by waiting for the last athlete before they all clap their hands.

Partner Sprint: In pairs, athletes will sprint up and down their lane, one D-Ball must be off the floor throughout the sprint. Females will use a 20kg and males will use a 30kg. The D-Ball can be switched at any point as long as athletes use their respective weights. One rep is there and back. Pairs can swap in and out as they wish.

title: One Zone Home WOD 55
subtitle: CrossFit One Zone Home WOD
workout:
EMOM for 16 minutes
Minute 1: 10 T-Push-Ups
Minute 2: 200 meter Run
Minute 3: 16 Alternating V-Ups
Minute 4: 60 Alternating Toe Taps

Repeat 4x
description: Background: “One Zone Home WOD 55” is from a collection of workouts designed by CrossFit One Zone @crossfitonezone (Esbly, France) to be done with minimal equipment. The series was posted during the 2020 COVID-19 pandemic when many athletes around the world were forced to work out at home with little or no equipment.
notes:
On a 16-minute clock, every minute on the minute ("EMOM") perform the prescribed work for that minute, then rest until the top of the minute. For example, from 0:00-1:00, perform 10 T Push-Ups and rest in the remaining time. From 1:00-2:00, perform the 200 meter Run and rest in the remaining time. Continue in this manner until 4:00, when 1 minute is allowed to complete 60 Alternating Toe Taps. Complete 4 total rounds of all 4 exercises.

Score is the total number of reps completed before the 16-minute clock stops.

Movement Standards

T-Push-Up: This is a variation of the standard Push-Up wherein athlete performs a Push-Up then raises one arm perpendicular to the ground to form a T-shape. Athlete places the raised hand on the ground again and perform another Push-Up and raises the other arm perpendicular to the ground. Each Push-Up counts as one rep.

Alternating Toe Tap: Place an object like a Dumbbell or Kettlebell in front of you. You can also use a plate or anything that can elevate you from the ground. Tap that object with your toes alternatingly as fast as possible.

title: They See Me Rollin, They See Me Lifting
subtitle: 2021 Battle Cancer London WOD #3
workout:
AMRAP (in a Team of 4) in 9 minutes
3 Rounds of:
20 Sandbag Over the Wall (30/20 kg, 1.58 m, 2 athletes)
Resting pair Holding the Worm Off the Ground (40 kg)

Worm Carry to end of lane (40 kg, 2 athletes)

10 Synchronised Over the Worm Burpees (40 kg, 4 athletes)
Roll Worm Back to Wall (40 kg, 2 athletes)
 
In Remaining time, AMRAP of:
Worm Carry and Roll Lengths (40 kg)
description: Background: “They See Me Rollin, They See Me Lifting” was the 3rd of the 4 total WODs for the 2021 Battle Cancer London competition. It was the 5th annual fundraising competition for cancer research and charities.
notes:
Athletes start lying on the ground in a line. On 3, 2, 1 Go, 2 athletes run out with the Sandbags (20kg for females, 30kg for males) and perform 20 Sandbag Over the Wall. Mixed teams will need to swap sides of the wall to stay with their respective weights. The resting pair will be holding the worm off the ground for the reps to count. Athletes can swap in and out as they wish.

Once completed, 2 athletes will carry the Worm on their shoulders to the end of the lane across the line, all 4 athletes will then complete 10 Synchro Over the Worm Burpees, before 2 athletes rolling the Worm back to the wall. In the remaining time, AMRAP Worm Carry and Roll lengths, with 2 athletes carrying up the lane and 2 athletes rolling it back down. Athletes can swap in and out as they wish.

Score is the total number of repetitions completed before the 9-minute clock stops.

Movement Standards

Sandbag Over Wall: Athletes will pick up the Sandbag with two hands and either by one motion or getting it to their laps first, will stand up with the Sandbag so it is at a height to throw over the wall. Athletes will work You Go, I Go, taking it in turns, however can swap as they wish with the resting athletes. Mixed teams must follow their sandbag through the wall so they stay with their respective weights.

Worm Hold: The 2 resting athletes will hold the Worm up off the ground, whilst standing to full extension. Athletes can hold the worm in a Deadlift Hold, in a front rack, or on the shoulders. By bending down 2 athletes working together will pick the Worm up grabbing the worm with both hands - 1 hand under, 1 hand over to either a deadlift height, up to chest height, or on to their shoulders by doing a full Worm Clean up to shoulder height. Athletes must be stood to full extension whilst holding the Worm in any of the variations.

Worm Carry: 2 athletes will Clean the Worm to their shoulders, by standing on the same side of the Worm, bending their knees, and grabbing the Worm with both hands - 1 hand under, 1 hand over. And in one motion cleaning the Worm to their shoulders. Athletes will then face down the lane and run/walk with the Worm to the other end. Athletes can swap in and out as they wish, and can do so without dropping the Worm each time.

Synchronized Burpee Over Worm: Athletes will start the rep standing up in 1 line facing the Worm, athletes will jump down to the floor in one motion finishing with their chest touching the floor. Athletes will then jump back up, and over the Worm. The synchronization is at the bottom when all 4 athletes' chests are on the floor.

Worm Roll: 2 athletes will roll the Worm from one end of the lane to the other across the line. By staying on their feet, athletes will push the Worm with their hands to roll it, athletes can swap in and out as they wish as long as only 2 athletes are working at any one time.

title: Ascent
subtitle: 2017 CrossFit Southie Showdown WOD

1 rep max Snatch
description: "Ascent" was a WOD programmed by CrossFit Southie @crossfitsouthie (Boston, MA, USA) for their 2017 Southie Showdown. It was posted on their site on October 18, 2017.
notes:
One athlete will lift at a time, with a lift being performed every 15 seconds. Each athlete will get 3 attempts. Athletes can make multiple attempts at a lift within their 15-second interval, but the lift must be initiated (bar pulled from the floor) prior to the 15-second window ending. Athletes will have 3 minutes 15 seconds between each attempt.

Any type of snatch (power, split, squat) is allowed. At the top of the movement, athletes must be in full control with the feet under the hips and the bar stacked on top of the shoulders, hips and ankles. Dropping to a knee before standing up the lift will result in a no rep.

For safety reasons, if the bar goes out of an athlete’s lane at any point, the rep will not be counted. Athletes will be responsible for loading and changing weights. Clips must be used and spare plates must be placed out of the way in their designated spots before each attempted lift.

*Note: The smallest weights available will be 2.5lb plates, meaning weight jumps must be made in a minimum of 5-lb increments. Women will have a 35-lb Barbell for this event.

description: The 2017 CrossFit Team Series was a new format compared to prior years, designed for teams of two. Two women, two men or a man and a woman are allowed. 2017 was all about the twos: two-person teams took on two sets of workouts over two weeks. The event took place from Sept. 20 through Oct. 2. This eighth workout of the series was announced on September 27, 2017.
notes:
At the call of “3, 2, 1… go!” the athlete will grab the handle and row 1,000 meters. They will then move to the barbell for 50 thrusters, then to the pull-up bar for 30 chest-to-bar pull-ups. They will finish by slapping hands with the second athlete, who may then begin their row. The second athlete may be seated on the rower prior to the first athlete finishing their pull-ups, but the monitor must be reset to zero, and they may not grab the handle until after slapping hands. The second athlete will complete the row, thrusters and pull-ups in the same fashion as the first. This workout ends when the second athlete’s chest touches the bar on the last rep of the chest-to-bar pull-ups.
Every second counts in this workout. The team’s score will be the time it takes to complete all the repetitions. Time will be recorded in full seconds. Do not round up. If the team finishes in 12:32.7, its score is 12:32. There is no time cap. Note the time at which the first athlete finishes, as this will be required when submitting your score.

subtitle: Molon Labe CrossFit Memorial WOD
workout:
4 Rounds for Time
4 Rope Climbs (15 ft)
9 Wall Ball Sit-Ups (20/14 lb, 5 ft target)
12 Thrusters (100/70 lb)
400 meter Weighted Run*

Round 1 Run with plates (2x25/15 lb)
Round 2 Run with barbell (45/35 lb)
Round 3 Run with plates (2x25/15 lb)
Round 4 Run with barbell (45/35 lb)
description:
Background: In 1998, Mark Nolan, who owns Molon Labe CrossFit @molonlabecrossfit (Macedonia, Ohio), lost his 32-year-old sister Jennifer to domestic violence. She was shot and killed by her common-law partner.

Nolan says he designed this workout to "Celebrate Survivors and to End Domestic Violence," and named it as a tribute to his sister.

"'My mom showed up at my sister’s house to drop off my sister’s three kids and found her lying on the bathroom floor. He was still there at that point, up in the attic. She grabbed the kids and called the police, and when they got there, (her partner) shot and killed himself,' Nolan said.

"'That morning, she left me a voicemail basically just before she was killed. If I would have answered my phone, I would have talked to her. I couldn’t save her that day. I never got to give her a hug or say goodbye. It was something I battled with for a long time,' he said." - CrossFit Journal

From Mark: "The WOD is simply called “32” ... because my sister Jennifer lived 32 beautiful years on this earth. This workout is not only a tribute to her memory, but will tell a story. It will take the athlete through some of her life and it will bring many of the same feelings of struggle, hardship, and victories she experienced. It looks like a big workout, long and difficult to remember, yet when thinking back on my sister's life prior to her death she was raising 3 children, working full time in a hospital and taking 18 credit hours of college. So really we don’t have much here to deal with and remember.

There are 4 rounds of this WOD and it includes 4x 400 meter runs ... one of the events my sister participated in during her track and field career. Jennifer loved to run and jump and had set many records doing so. As children growing up in north east Pennsylvania we were surrounded by trees and we loved to climb. Therefore the rope climbs are reminiscent of those happy times.
 
Her youngest daughter, Haley, was 4 years old at the time so 4 rope climbs per round. Jennifer’s middle child Kendal was 9 and I added 9 wall ball sit-ups to a 5’ target. Matthew was her oldest at 12 [for the] Thrusters.

During each of the running portions of the WOD you will notice the plates and bar get disassembled and different items are taken and carried. This symbolizes the continual disassembly of the 3 children’s lives and Jennifer would need to carry them from time to time. She would give anything for their safety and security. Although at times they did not want to and this disassembly of the family sometimes is so difficult to put back together...but we have to do it. You bring the plates and bar back together as one unit.

Jennifer would have loved CrossFit. She would have loved the camaraderie and competition of the sport. She would have loved all of you. The community that is willing to bond together for someone they have never met to try and help make a difference in another person’s life. You are saving lives. Know that there will be points during this WOD you will want to quit but just remember that it’s not about you, it’s about Jennifer’s life. She never quit especially when things became difficult. When you reassemble the bar and plates on that final round of 32 and stand on the box. Know that you have victory, and know that you have helped save someone’s life and know that Jennifer would be so proud of you."

The workout was originally performed at Molon Labe CrossFit on September 7, 2013 as part of a fundraiser benefitting the Battered Women's Shelter of Akron, OH.
notes: Start with the bar and plates assembled. Each round for the run athlete must disassemble the bar and plates and run with the specified item(s) for the 400 meter run/carry. After completing each of the 4 rounds the bar and plates must be reassembled. Athlete must then finish on top of a 24” plyo box to stop the clock.
creator: Mark Nolan

description:
This Firefighter Hero WOD from 555 Fitness is dedicated to Karl Joseph, FDNY, Engine 207, who was killed on September 11, 2001.

Karl Joseph was a "probie," a probationary firefighter, at Engine Company 207 in downtown Brooklyn after joining the department in October 2000. The senior guys played pranks on him but he took it well. "When you're a probie, you really can't respond back to the veterans," said Michael Beehler, a firefighter who went through the fire academy with Mr. Joseph and worked with him at 207. "Karl had a way of shrugging off the ribbing. He had a great smile and a great laugh," Mr. Beehler said. "As far as the job, he was top-notch."

Born November 5, 1985, Mr. Joseph would have turned 26 the year he was killed. He was a native of Haiti. His parents fled the chaotic country with their nine children to stake their claim in America, said Lucy Bouciquot, a family friend. "He liked Haiti," she said, "but America was his home."

notes:
With a running clock, complete 5 rounds of the prescribed work in the order written as fast as possible ("For Time").

Score is the time on the clock when the last round of the Power Cleans is completed.

Tips and Strategy

Make time at the end of the specific warm-up to allow your athletes to build up to a heavy Hang Power Clean double. We suggest about 8:00 to build to a heavy Hang Power Clean double (not a max), just heavier than athletes would use in the workout. And then spend the remaining time of the specific warm-up dialing down the weight for the workout.

If you decide to perform the heavy lift, then you will need to cut out the accessory to allow for some cooldown and clean up time. 185/125 lb weights can be misleading. They indicate a need to use a weight that is at the upper end of moderate. With weights in this category we should be able to repeat singles, never fail a rep, and perform 5 reps unbroken.

If athletes can’t get their toes all the way to the Rings, but still want to try this movement have them perform multiple reps of a Kipping Knee Raise or attempt to bring their feet as high as possible. This will also help them develop capacity kipping on the Rings for other movements.

title: Row, Skip, Thrust
subtitle: 2022 Festivus Games WOD #3
workout:
For Time
700 meter Row
140 Double-Unders
28 Single-Arm Dumbbell Thrusters (2x50/35 lb)

Time Cap: 8 minutes
description: Background: “Row, Skip, Thrust” (a.k.a. “Festivus Games 22.3”) was the 3rd of 4 WODs for the 2022 Festivus Games. Festivus Games was designed so it wouldn’t be necessary to scale the events. No athlete, whether six months in or brand new, will need to scale any of the events. The competition is about capacity more than a high degree of skill.
notes:
On 3-2-1-Go! the athlete will begin the Row. After completing the Row the athlete will perform either Double-Unders (DU). It's the athlete's choice but whatever the athlete chooses they must stick with that skip modality for all of the reps. After completing the required skips the athlete will perform the required Single-Arm Dumbbell Thrusters, using either hand as they want, switching as they want, if at all.

Score is the time on the clock when the last Dumbbell Thruster is completed.

Movement Standards

Row: The athlete's feet do not have to be strapped in. The damper can be whatever the athlete chooses. Don't touch the handle before the MC says "Go."

Double-Under: This is the standard Double-Under in which the rope passes completely under the feet twice for each jump. The rope must spin forward for the rep to count.

Single-Arm Dumbbell Thruster: The Single-Arm Dumbbell Thruster always begins with the Dumbbell on the ground and no hand touching it. The first rep begins with the athlete gripping the Dumbbell handle with one hand, and by any method, lifting the Dumbbell to front-rack/shoulder height. The Dumbbell must remain at front-rack/shoulder height throughout the thruster reps.

Only one hand can ever touch the Dumbbell. With the Dumbbell in position the athlete lowers their hips to below the top of the knees and then, while always maintaining grip, rises and thrusts the Dumbbell to full lockout overhead, with the hips, knees and active arm fully extended, and the Dumbbell directly over the body midline. The athlete chooses when or whether to switch hands. There is no predefined requirement for switching.

If the Dumbbell is ever lower than front-rack height, it must be re-lifted from the ground to at least front-rack height before continuing. The first rep CAN be a Squat Clean into a Thruster.

Scaling Options

For Time
700 meter Row
210 Single-Unders
28 Single-Arm Dumbbell Thrusters (2x35/20 lb)

Time Cap: 8 minutes

subtitle: Hero WOD
workout:

description:
Background: This workout is dedicated to Corporal Brian Neil Calvin Pinksen who died at Landstuhl Regional Medical Center in Germany of wounds sustained eight days earlier on August 22, 2010 in Afghanistan.

He was a corporal, 2nd Battalion, The Royal Newfoundland Regiment, based in Corner Brook, NL. He was a reservist deployed with the 1st Battalion, The Royal Canadian Regiment Battle Group serving with the Canadian contingent of NATO forces in Afghanistan.

He and another soldier were injured when an improvised explosive device detonated during a routine foot patrol near Nakhonay, in the Panjwai district, southwest of Kandahar City. They were treated by medics at the scene, evacuated by helicopter to the hospital at Kandahar Airfield and then moved on August 25 to Germany for further treatment. Cpl Pinksen's his mother and girlfriend were at his bedside when he passed away.

Aged 21, Pinksen was from Sop's Arm, NL born on April 5, 1990. He finished school in Corner Brook. He joined the reserves while still in high school. He took part in infantry training at Canadian Forces Base Gagetown in New Brunswick and in 2009 at Fort Pickett, a U.S. Army National Guard base in Virginia. He deployed on his first operational tour of duty to Afghanistan in May 2010. Described as mature and well-liked, he loved to hunt, exercise and being outdoors. He was a fun-loving prankster with a great sense of humour.

He received the General Campaign Star – South-West Asia and the Sacrifice Medal.

Cpl Pinksen leaves behind his mother Debbie Pinksen, younger brothers Brandon and Blair Pinksen, father Neil Pinksen, girlfriend Natasha Burton, grandparents Calvin and Millicent Gillingham and Ross and Gertie Pinksen, large extended family and many friends.

The workout was designed by Tyler Smith, CF-L1, @tysmithcf.

The rep scheme signifies:
- 20 minutes for his age when he passed away
- 1,990/4/5 reps for his birthday.
notes:

Score is the total number of rounds and repetitions completed before the 20-minute clock stops.

description:
This Firefighter Hero WOD is dedicated to Joseph Farrelly, FDNY, Division 1, who was killed on September 11, 2001.

He had a penchant for historical biographies, an affinity for Bruce Springsteen and a weakness for romance. He loved his wife and children and his job with the New York City Fire Department.

In retrospect, some might call it prophetic that Capt. Joseph D. Farrelly would leave a note on his wife's pillow professing his love to her the night before he went missing in the World Trade Center catastrophe -- as if it foreshadowed the impending disaster he would confront.

But for the 47-year-old firefighter with a brave face and a soft heart, writing love letters to his wife was as natural as waking up in the morning and fixing her lunch. She would often find a note waiting for her on the dashboard of her car, by the bathroom sink or under a magnet on the refrigerator. "I can't begin to tell you how much I love you. Words are inadequate," he wrote before embarking on a 24-hour shift. "Already I can't wait to get home. Hope you had a good time today. Love you. Joe."

After scribbling that short message on Sept. 10, Mr. Farrelly left his Prince's Bay home for Engine Co. 4 at the South Street Seaport firehouse in Manhattan. His wife hasn't seen him since, and now her husband's last missive waits to be framed.

title: #BylerStrong
subtitle: CrossFit 234 Tribute WOD
workout:
AMRAP (with a Partner) in 32 minutes
Max Calorie Bike

Station1:
4 Rope Climbs

Station 2:
12 Thrusters (95/65 lb)
200 meter Medicine Ball Run (20/14 lb)

Station 3:
89 Double-Unders

One athlete should be on the Bike at all times. Switch after every station is completed.
description:
Background: This workout is dedicated to Brett Byler who was diagnosed in 2021 with glioblastoma, an aggressive and terminal form of brain cancer.

Born on April 12, 1989, Brett served his country as a proud US Marine, and was a police officer since 2009 with the Department of Defense, San Diego Police Department, and the Escondido Police Department. 

The workout was designed by CrossFit 234 @crossfit_234 (Dumfries, VA, USA) where Brett's sister, Brittany Byler Estes @brittbestes is a member.

Brittany’s brothers would always host a family and friends workout at her older brother’s property, and was described as a "CrossFit beast." They would complete stations of work, and collect a rock from a pile after having finished a hill run following each movement they chose for the stations. At the end of the workout, they’d tally up the rocks for their score. 

To honor Brett in another way, this workout includes “The Ride Without a Finish Line”. Brett’s last bike ride ended in a fall, which led to his diagnosis of glioblastoma. At the time of creating this workout, "Brett is still fighting his last fight, and Brittany has vowed to finish his last bike ride."

Brett’s last bike ride actually has no finish line. So long as we honor and learn from his bravery, kindness, and undying spirit, carrying it on to everyone we meet in this life, Brett’s last ride will never end. -CrossFit 234

The rep scheme signifies:
- 32 minutes for Brett's age when he was diagnosed
- 4/12/89 reps for his birthday.
notes:
On a 32-minute clock, complete as many repetitions as possible ("AMRAP") of the prescribed work in the order written. A partner will be on the bike at all times. While Partner A bikes for Calories, Partner B performs Station 1. Partner B will take a Medicine Ball with them on a 200 meter Run, and deposit the Ball at the halfway point.

Upon returning, Partner B then takes over Biking for Calories while Partner A completes Station 1, followed by a 200 meter Run, collecting the Medicine Ball deposited by their partner. Partner A will accumulate as many Medicine Balls as possible, and both partners together will accumulate a total number of calories biked during the 32:00 AMRAP.

There will be two scores for this workout. Score A is the total number of calories biked. Score B is the total number of Medicine Balls collected.

description:
Background: This workout is dedicated to Master Trooper Kevin Keith Conner, B-551, who was shot and killed while conducting a traffic stop of a speeding vehicle on U.S. 701, near Sellers Town Road, in Columbus County, North Carolina on October 17, 2018.

The subject opened fire on Trooper Conner as he was approaching the stopped vehicle, fatally wounding him. The man fled but was located near Fair Bluff. He lead officers on a pursuit until his vehicle became disabled on railroad tracks in the town. He then fled on foot but was located and taken into custody at 4:00 am.

A good samaritan happened upon Trooper Conner less than five minutes after he was shot and called 911. He was rushed to a nearby hospital where he was pronounced dead.

Trooper Conner had served with the North Carolina Highway Patrol for 11 years and had previously served with the North Carolina Marine Patrol. In 2011, he saved a driver's life when he extinguished a fire in the man's car after being involved in an accident.

He is survived by his wife and two children. 

This workout was designed by fellow Trooper R. B. Graves.

The rep scheme signifies:
- 10-17-18 reps for the date when Trooper Conner passed
- 551 meters for his badge number.

title: Calvario
subtitle: CrossFit Mentana Benchmark WOD
workout:
Three 6-minute AMRAPs in 24 minutes

AMRAP in 6 minutes:
5 Sumo Deadlift High-Pulls (60/40 kg)
10 Hang Squat Cleans (60/40 kg)
15 Push Presses (60/40 kg)

Rest 3 minutes

Then, AMRAP in 6 minutes:
50 Double-Unders
100 meter Shuttle Sprint
250 meter Row

Rest 3 minutes

Then, AMRAP in 6 Minutes:
15 Pull-Ups
30 Box Jump-Overs  (60/50 cm)
45 Air Squats
description:
Background: This workout, designed by coach Giovanni Volante of CrossFit Mentana @crossfitmentana (near Rome, Italy), was submitted to WODwell on April 12, 2017. Volante said in his submission, "We are in the Holy Week and the Passion. I needed a workout that put my athletes to the test in all three training modes of our sport, but at the same time as if they were three distinct workouts. What better time to think of Calvario, where the three crosses were placed. That's where we derive the three mini 6-minute WODs to give the right intensity." Giovanni chose a 2:1 work to rest ratio to allow the athlete "go and touch as much as possible for all 10 general physical skills."

The workout was inspired by the "Three Wise Men" WOD, a format that Giovanni says "I use from time to time to create intense and demanding WODs which I usually program later in the month on Saturday. I'll call them the workout of the week/month. When my athletes read WOW or WOM, know they have to roll up their sleeves and sweat a little more than usual. I personally scored 223 points RX. I know it's not much but at age 49 I can not complain."
notes: Complete all three AMRAPs including rest between each with a running clock. Score is the total number of points for all three parts. For the first and third AMRAPs, assign one point per rep. For the second AMRAP, assign one point for every 10 reps (eg: 50 DU = 5; 100 Shuttle Sprint = 10; 250 meter Rowing = 25).

These are treated as three separate events but must be completed within a 12-hour window. The workout begins with the runner standing behind the starting cone, or similar object. When the runner is ready, the clock will begin and the runner may begin the course. The athlete will run out 200 meters to a pre-measured turnaround point where they will go around the marker and pick up one Barbell collar.

They will then return to the starting point going around the cone, drop the collar then continue this course for three additional laps picking up a collar each time they go around the turnaround point. The time will stop when the runner crosses the starting line after the fourth lap.

For the Front Squat, the workout begins with the athlete standing at full extension with the Barbell loaded and in the squat rack. When the athlete is ready, they will take the bar from the squat rack in the front rack position and back the weight out of the rack. The athlete must clearly establish a starting position with the knees and hips fully extended and the Bar resting in the front rack position.

When the athlete is ready they will squat the Bar down to a position where the crease of the hip is clearly below the top of the knee and then return to the standing position with the knees and hips fully extended and the bar in the front rack position. The athlete will be given credit for the lift when they reach a position where the Bar is securely sitting in the front rack position with the hips and knees fully extended. The athlete should be facing the camera.

For the Strict Pull-Up, the workout begins with the athlete hanging from the Pull-Up Bar with full extension of the shoulders and elbows with the feet off the ground. When the athlete is ready they will pull themselves up a position where the chin is clearly above the bar and then return to the starting position. The athlete will continue this process until they have completed the maximum number of repetitions they can do. The event ends when either one or both hands comes off of the Bar or the feet touch the ground. Kipping or butterfly-style chin-ups are not permitted.

There will be three scores for this challenge. Each event will be scored individually. Score A is the time it takes to complete the 1 mile Run. Score B is the heaviest load successfully lifted for the Front Squat. Score C is the total number Unbroken Pull-Ups completed.

Movement Standards

Run: The athlete will start behind the starting cone or similar object. When the athlete is ready, they will run a pre-measured course that is 200 meters out and 200 meters back. 4 "out and back" laps will need to be completed for the 1 mile Run. The athlete must Run around the cone, or a similar object at both ends of the 200m course. The athlete must pick up and bring back 1 collar from the turnaround point on each lap, the collar will simply be thrown to the ground when turning around at starting point. The collars can be placed on the ground or on an elevated object as long as they are easily accessible for the runner.

Front Squat: This is a traditional Front Squat with the loaded Barbell starting in the squat rack. When the athlete is ready, they will take the Barbell from the squat rack and establish a front rack position with the knees and hips fully extended and the Barbell resting in the front rack position. When the athlete is ready they will squat the load down to a position where the hip crease in clearly below the top of the knee and then return the Barbell to the standing position where the hips and knees are fully extended.

Strict Pull-Up: This is a Chin-Up where the grip on the Pull-Up Bar is supinated. The palms of both hands must be facing the athlete's face. The athlete starts hanging freely from the Pull-Up Bar with the feet clearly off the ground. When the athlete is ready they will execute as many repetitions as possible without either hand coming off the Bar or the feet touching the ground

A repetition will count when the athlete pulls themselves from a position with the shoulders and elbows clearly extended to a position where the chin is clearly above the Bar. Kipping Chin-Ups are not permitted. Kipping, hitching or any use of the legs or hips to aid the chin up will invalidate that repetition - this is a strict movement.

The attempt will end as soon as either hand comes free of the Pull-Up Bar, or either of the feet touch the ground. The athlete may hang freely on the Bar as long as they want to between repetitions as long as the feet do not touch the ground, and both hands remain in contact with the Bar.

title: PSD Dutch
subtitle: Element CrossFit Hero WOD
workout:
For Time
Buy-In: 67 Burpees

Then, 5 Rounds of:

17 Sandbag Squats (70 lb)
21 Push-Ups
23 Sandbag Box Step-Ups (20 in, 70 lb)

Rest 2 minutes

Cash-Out: 800 meter Sandbag Run (70 lb)

Wear a Weight Vest (20/14 lb)
description:
Background: This workout is dedicated to PSD Dutch while on duty on August 26, 2021. 5-year-old Dutch was entering the prime of his career before suffering a medical episode related to an undiagnosed heart condition.

Colin Manson was PSD Dutch’s handler. He has 22 years of policing experience in a varying number of areas and is a well-experienced and well-respected officer. He joined the K9 Unit in 2017 where he was partnered with Dutch for the entire time until he passed. They went through their Basic Handler Course where they became certified in their Patrol Work Function. Later on, Dutch became certified in Drug and Firearm detection. In total, they attended and assisted in 650 calls for service.

The workout was designed by Peel Police K9 Unit with the assistance of Coach Alex Bibiri of Element CrossFit @elementcrossfit (Ontario, Canada).

The rep scheme signifies:
- 67 Burpees for the number of arrests
- 5 rounds for Dutch's age when he passed
-17 Sandbag Squats for the year he came into service
- 9 Pull-Ups for the month of Dutch's passing
- 21 Push-Ups for the year of his passing
- 23 Sandbag Box Step-Ups for the first two digits of Colin's Badge
- 2 minute Rest for Dutch's badge
- 800 meter Sandbag Run for how long his track was.
notes:
With a running clock, complete the prescribed work in the order written as fast as possible ("For Time"). Athlete must start with the buy-in of 67 Burpees, then proceed to 5 rounds of 9 Pull-Ups, 17 Sandbag Squats, 21 Push-Ups, and 23 Sandag Box Step-Ups. Rest 2 minutes before completing the Cash-Out of 800-meter Sandbag Run.

Score is the time on the clock when the cash-out is completed.

title: Regionals 9.1 (Canada West)
subtitle: 2009 CrossFit Games Regionals WOD
workout:
AMRAP in 20 minutes

description:
Background: By 2009, interest in the sport of fitness had grown to the point where a qualification step was necessary. On September 26, 2008, the 2008 Games site warned:

“The 2009 Games will not be open enrollment. There will be no scaling. You must qualify to enter. Adequate performance in the 2008 Games will count. There will be a series of qualifying events around the country (world) in May, 2009.”

For individual competitors, the 2009 CrossFit Games season was a two-step process: Regionals and the Games. It was the only CrossFit Games season that included a two-step process. 2007 and 2008 were one-stage competitions, and each year since 2009 has featured three stages.

The Regionals began with the now familiar breakdown of the world into 17 Regions. The names and boundaries, however, were different. Instead of the now familiar South East, you had the Dirty South. Much of what we now know as South Central went by the name of Hell’s Half Acre. And the tiny island of Iceland had its own Regional, separate from the rest of Europe.

Regional programming in 2009 featured creative flair, as well. Each Regional had separate qualification workouts, opening the door for some innovation. Canada East featured a cross-country run over “rough” terrain with stops for “mini-events” along the way. The North West Regional brushed off an old classic long discontinued in Olympic weightlifting competitions — the clean and press. NorCal required uphill farmer’s walks, with the unexpected complication of heavy rain.

In addition to the 17 live Regionals, individuals qualified for the Games in 2009 via the Last Chance Online Qualifier, a virtual, video submission competition. Foreshadowing the CrossFit Games Open, the Last Chance Qualifier posted three workouts and had competitors complete them on their own and submit results and videotaped performances via email. Athletes who missed qualification at Regionals had a second chance at making the Games. Surprisingly, the 2009 CrossFit Games’ second-place finisher, Tommy Hackenbruck qualified via the Last Chance Qualifier, as did Peter Egyed and Spencer Hendel.

The first of 3 total workouts for the 2009 Canada West CrossFit Games Regionals (aka: "Regionals 9.1 (Canada West)") was announced on May 3, 2009.

description:
Background: 2010 again redesigned the CrossFit Games season. On December 3, 2009, the Games site announced that the 2010 Regionals would no longer be open to anyone — athletes would have to qualify via Sectionals, a new stage of competition. Sectionals chopped the world up into even smaller bits. Some regions were split into as many as four different sections. In addition, an Online Qualifier, specifically designed for military service members unable to attend Sectionals, fed athletes into Regionals.

While 2010 saw the Sectionals spread out over the world, the number of Regionals decreased. Canada East and West were consolidated into one Canada Regional, and Iceland joined Europe. In total, 13 live Regional competitions selected the athletes of the CrossFit Games. Similar to 2009, each qualifying event for the CrossFit Games featured different programming during both Sectionals and Regionals.

The last of 5 total workouts for the 2010 Canadian CrossFit Games Regionals (aka: "Regionals 10.5 (Canada)") was announced on May 26, 2010.

title: Maria Felipe de Oliveira
subtitle: CrossFit Porto Seguro Memorial WOD
workout:
For Time

description:
Background: This workout is dedicated to Maria Felipa de Oliveira. Translated from Portuguese via the submitter of the workout, Oliveira was "the black heroine from the Independence of Brazil in Bahia. Born on the island of Itaparica, she had the function of observing the movement of the caravels and then passing on the information to the Liberation Movement Command."

"Tired of the role of lookout, she went into combat and led a group of about 200 people, including black women and Indians, responsible for burning more than 40 Portuguese vessels. This action was decisive for the victory over the Portuguese in Salvador. She died on January 4, 1873."

The workout was designed by Hiero Horta @hierohortacoach, owner and head coach, of CrossFit Porto Seguro @crossfitps (Porto Seguro, Brazil).

The rep scheme signifies:
- 200 Alternating Lunges for the approximate number of people who joined Maria in the struggle for freedom
- 40 Chest-to-Bar Pull-Ups for the number of women in the fight and also the number of Portuguese vessels destroyed
- 4 rounds for the day when Maria died
- 1 Legless Rope Climb for the month when she passed
- 18 and 73 reps for the year.
notes:

Score is the time on the clock when the buy-out is completed.

title: Semifinals 21.5
subtitle: 2021 CrossFit Games Online Semifinals WOD #5
workout:
For Time
2,000 meter Row
60 meter Handstand Walk
5 Legless Rope Climbs

1,000 meter Row
40 meter Handstand Walk
4 Legless Rope Climbs

500 meter Row
20 meter Handstand Walk
3 Legless Rope Climbs

Time Cap: 30 minutes
description:
Background: “Semifinals 21.4” is the 5th of the 6 total workouts for the CrossFit Online Semifinals competition. 

The CrossFit Online Semifinals is the final qualifying stage for athletes who qualified for The Atlas Games, German Throwdown, CrossFit Asia Invitational, CrossFit Lowlands Throwdown, and Brazil CrossFit Championship  before the 2021 NOBULL CrossFit Games. Only the top 5 of each competition will make it to the Games.
notes:
Prior to starting the workout, set up the workout area as shown in the floor plan. The camera must be placed on the same side as the rower, and the monitor must be clearly visible. The Rope must be on the opposite side of the Rower.

This workout begins with the athlete seated on the Rower with their hands at their sides, clearly off the paddle. At “3, 2, 1 … go,” the athlete will complete a 2,000-meter Row, then 60 meters of Handstand Walking, changing directions after every 5 meters, and then 5 Legless Rope Climbs. They will continue this sequence with a 1,000-meter Row, 40-meter Handstand Walk, and 4 Legless Rope Climbs, then finally a 500-meter Row, 20-meter Handstand Walk, and 3 Legless Rope Climbs. Time stops when the athlete touches above the 15-foot mark, completing the final Legless Rope Climb.

Score is the total time taken to complete the event or the total number of repetitions completed at the time cap. There is no tiebreak for this event.

Movement Standards

Rower: The monitor on the Rower must be set to zero at the beginning of the row. Athletes may have assistance resetting the Rower between rounds. The athlete must stay seated on the Rower with their hands holding the paddle until the monitor reads at least the designated distance. If the athlete reaches the time cap on the Rower, every 100 meters completed when the Rower comes to rest will count as a rep (rounded down, e.g., 475 meters = 4 reps).

Handstand Walk: When kicking up, the hands (including the fingers) must be placed on the ground BEHIND the line designating the 5-meter segment. Placing the hands on or over the line when kicking up constitutes a no rep. Each 5-meter segment will count as 1 rep. Both hands, including palms and fingers, must touch the ground completely clear of the line marking the end of the 5-meter segment before the feet touch the ground. If at any time the athlete comes down from their hands before finishing a 5-meter segment, they must repeat the entire segment. Athletes are not required to kick down after completing a segment but MUST change directions after completing each 5-meter increment.

Legless Rope Climb: Each rep starts with both feet on the ground. Each rep starts with both feet on the ground. The rep is credited when one hand clearly touches above the designated 15-foot mark. Athletes may choose to touch a fixed object, such as a beam or the ceiling, so long as the object is at least 15 feet high. Only after the athlete has clearly made the touch at the top of the climb can they use their legs to descend the Rope. There are no additional requirements during the descent of the climb.

Scaling Options

This is a long, high-skill workout. Deconditioned athletes should reduce the overall volume and choose gymnastics modifications that incorporate time on hands as well as a pull.

title: Semifinals 21.3
subtitle: 2021 CrossFit Online Semifinals WOD #3
workout:
For Time
30 Muscle-Ups
30 meter Dumbbell Front Rack Lunges (2x50/35 lb)
300 Double-Unders

20 Muscle-Ups
20 meter Dumbbell Front Rack Lunges (2x50/35 lb)
200 Double-Unders

10 Muscle-Ups
10 meter Dumbbell Front Rack Lunges (2x50/35 lb)
100 Double-Unders

Time Cap: 25 minutes
description:
Background: “Semifinals 21.3” is the 3rd of the 6 total workouts for the CrossFit Online Semifinals competition. 

The CrossFit Online Semifinals is the final qualifying stage for athletes who qualified for The Atlas Games, German Throwdown, CrossFit Asia Invitational, CrossFit Lowlands Throwdown, and Brazil CrossFit Championship  before the 2021 NOBULL CrossFit Games. Only the top 5 of each competition will make it to the Games.
notes:
Prior to starting the workout, set up the workout area as shown in the floor plan. The Dumbbells must always be returned behind the line furthest from the Rings.

This workout begins with the athlete standing on the far side of the 5-meter zone furthest from the Rings. At “ 3, 2, 1 … go,” the athlete will move to the Rings to complete 30 Muscle-Ups, then to the Dumbbells to complete 30 meters of Dumbbell Front Rack Lunges, changing direction after each 5-meter segment. Then they will complete 300 Double-Unders. They will continue in this fashion for 20 Muscle-Ups, 20 meters of Dumbbell Front Rack Lunges, 200 Double-Unders, and then 10 Muscle-Ups, 10 meters of Dumbbell Front Rack Lunges, and 100 Double Unders. Time stops after the completion of the final Double-Under.

Score is the total time it takes to complete the workout or the total number of repetitions completed at the time cap. There is no tiebreak for this event.

Movement Standards

Muscle-Up: Athletes must begin each rep hanging from the Rings, with arms fully extended and feet off the ground. Kipping is allowed, but uprises and swings/rolls to support are not permitted. During consecutive kipping Muscle-Ups, a change of direction below the rings is required. No part of the foot may rise above the bottom of the rings during the kip. The athlete must pass through some portion of a dip before reaching lockout. The rep is credited when the elbows are fully locked out in the support position. Reaching lockout while pushing or falling away from the rings will not count.

Dumbbell Front Rack Lunge: The athlete must start each 5-meter length with both feet clearly behind the line. Each Lunge begins with the Dumbbells at the shoulders, feet together, and hips and legs extended.  The Dumbbells must remain at the shoulders. A full grip around the handle of the Dumbbell must be maintained for the duration of the Lunge. Resting the Dumbbells on the shoulders is allowed. Releasing the grip on the handle and letting the Dumbbell rest solely on the shoulder is not allowed.

The trailing knee must make contact with the ground at the bottom of each Lunge before returning to full hip and leg extension. The athlete must alternate which foot leads for each rep. Stopping with both feet together at the top of each rep is not required, but both legs must be fully extended if the athlete chooses to step through at the top. Shuffle steps that advance the athlete forward between reps are not allowed.

Each 5-meter length will be considered 1 rep. The rep is credited when: - both heels are past the line (touching the line will not count), the feet are together, and the hips and legs are fully extended. The athlete must reach the finish position before lowering the Dumbbells from the shoulders. Lunging more than 5 meters in one direction without turning around is not allowed. If the athlete fails to meet any standard during a step, including not touching the trailing knee to the ground, not reaching full extension at the top of the rep, or not keeping the Dumbbells at the shoulders for the duration of the rep, the athlete must repeat the entire 5-meter length.

Double-Under: The athlete must remain behind the tape line. If the athlete’s feet touch or cross the line at any time, the rep will not count.  The rope passes under the feet twice for each jump. The rope must spin forward for the rep to count. Only successful jumps are counted, not attempts. Athletes may NOT have assistance resetting their equipment during the workout.

Scaling Options

Modify the Muscle-Ups to pull and push exercises that challenge you without causing you to hit failure. Newer athletes should reduce the overall volume of this workout.
